exposure: failure of an immune compromised patient to fight infection
increased duration of second stage of labour
cohort: The study included 4007 patients who delivered either vaginally with episiotomy/tear or by caesarean section, and patients undergoing laparotomy for ectopic pregnancies.
finding: Medical disorders (anaemia, hypothyroidism, diabetes, hypertension) and obstetric/surgical factors (increased duration of labour/second stage, surgery, rupture of membranes, and more vaginal examinations) were significantly associated with the development of surgical site infection.
mod_finding: The study reported surgical site infections occurring after both vaginal deliveries with episiotomy/tear (110 cases) and caesarean sections (132 cases), with increased duration of labour and surgery identified as risk factors for SSI.
